result.summary: This residential street features continuous sidewalks but lacks basic intersection infrastructure such as marked crosswalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps. The pedestrian environment is further degraded by sidewalk obstructions like trash bins and utility poles, as well as poor pavement quality.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crosswalks
hazards.description: There are no painted markings to indicate a safe crossing point for pedestrians at the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground intersection area

hazards.name: Missing Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The lack of sloped transitions at the corner creates a significant barrier for people with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the sidewalk in the foreground

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash cans and utility poles narrow the effective walking width of the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the sidewalk in front of the row houses

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the corner may block the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street near the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install tactile, sloped curb ramps at all corners of the intersection to ensure accessibility.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the intersection to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair and Maintenance
interventions.description: Repair cracked and uneven pavement sections to prevent tripping hazards.

result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with sidewalks but no marked crosswalks or visible traffic control devices. Large vegetation and parked vehicles create significant sightline obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross the wide, unmarked roadway.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection, forcing pedestrians to cross without a designated or protected space.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground intersection area

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Large bushes on the right corner and parked cars along the street block the view between approaching drivers and pedestrians at the curb.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground corner and along the street edges

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks to define pedestrian space and increase driver awareness.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces and trim vegetation near the intersection to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they enter the roadway.

result.summary: This residential street features a continuous sidewalk on the left side, but lacks any marked pedestrian crossings or traffic control infrastructure. The wide, unmarked roadway may encourage higher vehicle speeds, and the absence of curb ramps limits accessibility.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked areas for pedestrians to cross the street, increasing exposure risk.
hazards.location_in_image: Visible throughout the length of the roadway

hazards.name: Unmarked wide roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a wide residential street can lead to higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable positioning.
hazards.location_in_image: The asphalt roadway surface

hazards.name: Lack of curb ramps
hazards.description: The absence of curb ramps at potential crossing points creates a barrier for people with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: The curb line along the sidewalk on the left

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at intersections to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and sloped ramps at all crossing points to ensure accessibility.

interventions.title: Lane Markings and Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Add lane markings to define travel lanes and consider curb extensions or street trees to narrow the perceived roadway width.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential intersection with a one-way street and minimal pedestrian infrastructure. While a sidewalk is present, the environment lacks marked crosswalks, curb ramps, and traffic control devices for pedestrians.
